why: A's theorem_7_1_13 (∃ R : X.NaturalRep x, R.U ⊆ V) gives every clause of B's IsNatRepData directly from the NaturalRep fields (Φ(g⁻¹) as the inverse witness, Φ_mul for the homomorphism, Γ sc-smooth on U, (1)–(3)), with B's Gx (a subtype) and the project's Isotropy (a structure) identified and the products agreeing; B's 'i.e.' bijection is A's bijOn_Γ transported. The project's NaturalRep is a priori stronger than B's data in two ways: U is required to be connected (the text's theorem does not say so), and the inverse of Φ(g) must be Φ(g⁻¹). Neither is a genuine difference: Φ(1) = id on U follows from injectivity and idempotence, giving Φ(g⁻¹) as inverse, and U can be shrunk to the connected component of x in U, which is open (M-polyfolds are locally connected, MPolyfold.isOpen_connectedComponentIn) and Φ-invariant (each Φ(g) is a homeomorphism of U fixing x); so B ⇒ theorem_7_1_13. The other conjuncts (Φ_one, mapsTo_Φ, Φ_inv_Φ, bijOn_Γ) are facts about an arbitrary NaturalRep, re-proved outright from its fields. Universes at 0.
overlap: B_to_A: 118 shared project theorems — almost all generic M-polyfold/sc-calculus infrastructure reached through IsScSmoothOn.mono and MPolyfold.isOpen_connectedComponentIn (locallyConnectedSpace, locallyPathConnectedSpace, chart/retraction lemmas), plus groupoid axioms and NaturalRep field accessors; no Chapter 7 construction lemma (lemma_7_6_2, lemma_7_6_3, NatRepConstruction) is reused.
